subject: Animation
title: Jafar: The Power-Hungry Sorcerer
description: A micro-lesson that makes Jafar: The Power-Hungry Sorcerer usable.

hook.text: Jafar from Aladdin is designed entirely around vertical lines — tall, thin, and sharp like a dagger.

buildup.text: His character contrasts Aladdin's round, friendly design. Sharp equals threatening. Round equals trustworthy.

discovery.text: Jonathan Freeman voiced Jafar with silky menace, recording his lines alongside Robin Williams' manic Genie.

twist.text: Jafar's downfall comes from greed — he wishes to be all-powerful and gets trapped as a genie himself.

climax.text: Jafar demonstrated that villain design and hero design should be visual opposites to create instant contrast.

punchline.text: Every sharp line in Jafar's design tells you he is dangerous before he speaks.

quiz.question: How does Jafar's visual design contrast with Aladdin's?
options: Jafar uses bright colors while Aladdin uses dark colors
Jafar uses sharp vertical lines while Aladdin uses round friendly shapes — sharp equals threatening
They share the same design language to show their hidden similarities
